title: candles, built only from proof
body: token and pool pages now draw real candlesticks — TradingView's open-source Lightweight Charts, vendored so the bytes served are the bytes in the repository — over a token's whole life from its first verified trade. timeframes from 15m to 1d, volume underneath, and clicking any candle opens the transaction that closed it, because every candle is bucketed only from trades replayed against the market program's own formula. trades without a chain clock refuse to chart: a candle asserts a duration, and kascov does not invent time. the per-trade step line, every point a link to its transaction, stays one pill away. the API grew /candles and /book to match, both in the OpenAPI document.

title: the archive can no longer lie to itself
body: the worker now refuses to start against a missing database instead of silently creating an empty one — for the sole archive of mainnet covenant history, amnesia served as health was the worst failure mode there was. every systemd unit escalates failure to a webhook, the watchdog alerts before it self-heals, a weekly job restores an off-site backup and proves the restoration, and deploys must end with the running worker reporting the exact git hash just built — /healthz now carries it. this exists because a hand-run deploy silently rebuilt an old commit this very week; that class of incident is now structurally impossible.

title: eight audited builds, and a family of our own
body: the matcher now recognises eight builds under one discipline, and the newest is the closest to home: the KCM launch curve — the founder's own launchpad — pinned on exactly the terms every KRON family got. its sources are published and its compiler pinned, so the fixture is reproducible by anyone; recognising a family is not endorsing it. its resting limit orders are indexed too, because an order book is many cells and recognition is the difference between a book existing and not. matcher version 8 re-verifies every stored program, the unknowns board finally shows who pinned each family first, and a new exact-hash tier can recognise single-deployment builds — it ships empty, because publishing constants nobody audited would break the premise.

title: findable, at last
body: every route now carries its own title and canonical instead of one poetic page answering five addresses, search finds the listed names the site itself displays — with matched:listed provenance, never silently — changelog entries have permalinks the feed points at, pools pages resolve names like every other surface, and the passport's anchor lineage links to an explorer that can actually show the transactions. small screws, but every one of them sat between kascov and a new reader.

title: the whole token market has an API
body: the public API no longer stops at token summaries. every token can now be searched and paged with stable cursors, then opened for its holders, complete event history and verified trades. there is a global trade feed, a market directory covering bonding curves and graduated pools, and commitment-proven vesting schedules with their claim history. filters cover phase, pricing, side, token and market without turning exact integers into floats. every path is documented in the live API reference and OpenAPI document, and the JavaScript and Python clients speak it too. unverified programs still fail closed: they stay unpriced and out of the trade feed.

title: the matcher learns the third generation
body: KRON shipped a new build generation and kascov can now prove it: curve v3 is v2 plus the value-continuation fix announced on august 4, visible in the bytecode as three inserted copies of a nine-byte check ending in GREATERTHANOREQUAL VERIFY. pinned from three mainnet deployments, each recovered from its own spend and blake2b-proven against its P2SH commitment: 2,654 pushes, opcode gaps byte-identical across all three, the same 33 parameter roles as v2 at shifted positions. the pool it graduates into is pinned from the template the proven curve itself embeds, and the first v3-graduated mainnet pool matches it outside exactly the two creator slots. the matcher version bumps to 5, so every stored unmatched program gets re-read: Entity X, KREX and their siblings move from unknown to priced-and-verified on the next pass.

title: the passport touched mainnet
body: the anchor is live: a transaction from the published anchor address carries kascov:passport:v1:<root> in its payload, and /passport shows the green anchored state with the txid. the root re-anchors daily whenever it changes, and it already has, twice. a badge on any passport now verifies against raw chain bytes with no kascov server in the loop. reputation, notarized by the chain it lives on.

title: voting writes itself into your passport
body: closing a vote round now mints a participation claim for every ballot: voted-round-N, naming the round and nothing else. the choice is never stored and never published, ballots are still deleted at close, and nothing mints for rounds closed before today. the passport page also learned to tell the truth harder: until the mainnet anchor arms, the root lives only in the file this site serves, and the page now says exactly that.

title: the pocket fix
body: on a phone, an address page's copy button now sits where a thumb expects it, and the token tables stop letting a long name column swallow the screen: names compact, balances stay visible, and the sideways scroll actually shows you something.

title: the passport, the unknowns board, and the bench wire
body: three community programs land. the passport: every earned role becomes a claim keyed to your chain-proven address, merkleized, the root published, and the same verification ships in the js and py clients, so a badge checks out with zero trust in kascov's servers; the mainnet anchor arms next. the unknowns board lists every covenant build the bench cannot yet name, as open problems: pin one and the family carries your handle forever. and every monday the bench posts its week to the discord, whether or not anyone was watching.

title: the token learned its duties
body: the $KASCOV lanes are now real code: an audit vote where verified holders pick which unknown covenant family gets pinned next (one holder one vote, a public counts-only tally, and it can never touch a verdict), watchtower DMs that tell a holder when a held token changes phase or a balance crosses a line, and a holder lane that mints stateless API capacity from a signed message. the bot's terms page was re-audited sentence by sentence against the code, including the promise that leaving the server deletes your record. it does. and the kascov Discord is open: discord.gg/83RjgQBDEX

title: the token that cannot buy a verdict
body: kascov.io/token is the $KASCOV landing page: every number read live from the chain with a proof link beside it, graduation shown as a chain event, the doctrine as four cards, and the biggest box on the page is the one that tells you what the token does not do.

title: the searched coin steps forward
body: search the galaxy and the coin you asked for now grows into its own face and answers properly: a card pinned beside it reads its name and ticker, what kind of coin it is, and the market line the directory can prove — bonding progress, holders, lifetime trades. the card rides with the coin as you pan. every word on it is derived from chain or the signed list, never typed in by us.

title: the galaxy learned names and faces
body: search the galaxy for a token the way you actually know it: its name or ticker, claimed or listed, not just its covenant id. the match zooms to the coin and the label now reads both. once the camera is close, a token wears its own art, clipped into the node: chain-proven art and witnessed listed logos on the same tiers the rest of the site uses. identity is a client-side join keyed by covenant id, so the galaxy payload did not grow by a byte. and the community page now shows KRON, the first covenant DEX and launchpad on Kaspa L1, whose trades kascov replays against the programs' own bytecode.

title: the unknown queue starts auditing itself
body: everything mechanical about auditing an unknown build now runs on its own, every six hours, on both networks: recover each unmatched program from its own spend, prove it against its commitment, cluster programs into build families by structure, diff family members into per-deployment slots, and trial-replay every trade until a constant assignment explains the build with zero invariant breaks. the report lives in the verification log, ranked by how much activity rides on each family, with a proposed fixture per family. its first run recovered all 241 unknown programs on testnet and sorted them into 21 families, nine slots on the biggest. what it deliberately never does is promote: proposals are for a person to read and pin, because a verifier that approves builds nobody read would be worthless.

title: the second-generation KRON builds, audited and priced
body: KRON's new launches ran on builds kascov had never audited, so they sat honestly unpriced in the unknown queue. Seven deployments of the new curve were recovered from their own spends and blake2b-proven against their commitments: 2,645 pushes each, byte-identical outside exactly 33 positions, and every one of the 33 has a meaning, token id to graduation target. Two checks the old build never offered came free: the program states its own byte length ten times over, and it embeds two copies of the pool it graduates into, which must match. The new pool build is the same design as the old with the same 20 bps LP fee at the same position in its arithmetic, proven by replaying all 580 trades of the first market that graduated on it. And a vested launch finally finds its market: two covenants hold such a token from genesis, the market and the creator's lock, and the old unique-holder rule refused to choose. The holder whose program byte-matched an audited market build is now the market, which is how a token whose bonding completed shows its pool instead of an em dash.

title: every holder, trade and address leads to one page
body: holders now show a wallet address instead of 32 bytes of hex, and every trade names the address on the other side. open an address to see what it holds, with each token's art and ticker, what covenants it owns, and every trade it took. a key that only ever traded gets a page too, even holding nothing today. trade lists show all of them now rather than the newest 250, fetched when you ask for them. and any transaction says how kascov read it, side and amounts and both balances before and after, so a disagreement with another indexer has an answer instead of an argument.

title: a live map of who holds what
body: every token page draws its holders as a bubble map. area is the proven balance, so bags compare honestly instead of by width. a covenant holding a reserve is coloured apart from a wallet holding a bag, because those are not the same thing. drag any bubble and the rest re-pack around it, one solve per frame.

title: every verification pass is now on the record
body: kascov re-derives everything from chain, and now writes down each pass: what it examined, what it matched, what failed an invariant, and what it could not recognise at all. unmatched programs are queued by shape rather than by bytes, because a launchpad bakes different constants into every deployment, so the bytes never repeat but the structure always does. that collapses 223 unmatched covenants on testnet into 18 families you can actually work through. it is a queue to audit, never a ranking to trust, and none of it is priced. teaching the matcher a new build re-verifies the whole history rather than only what arrives next.

title: pools got pages, and a diagram of their own wiring
body: a graduated token's pool has its own page now, plus a directory of every pool. it draws the wiring it reads out of the pool's state block: the KAS reserve, the token reserve, and the covenant between them. the LP share token is named by its own bytecode and its holders are counted, and the 20 bps LP fee is treated as part of the formula rather than a violation of it. what kascov will not do is tell you how much of that liquidity is locked forever, because it cannot prove it. there is also a page listing what every badge on this site has to prove to be shown.

title: the audit panel: every check, its verdict, its reason
body: each token page carries a fixed 19-point checklist: every check kascov ran, whether it passed, and the exact reason when it did not. the list is the same length for every token, so one with nothing to hide and one that failed something look structurally identical and you read the verdicts instead of counting rows. one entry walks you through verifying a proof yourself.

title: prices, verified against the curve's own bytecode
body: the tokens directory shows a price in KAS, the reserve and 24h volume, and none of it comes from a launchpad API. kascov pulls every trade out of hash-proven state changes, proves each bonding-curve program against its own commitment, reads the curve constants from the committed bytes, and replays every trade through the program's own formula before publishing anything. a price appears only when the program matched a pinned build, its invariant held on every trade, and at least three real trades exercised its constants. there is deliberately no market cap: a marginal price times supply overstated the biggest token here by 13x, so kascov publishes exit value instead, capped by the KAS the covenant really holds. graduated pools price too, and each token shows its market phase. anything that cannot be proven stays blank, with the reason on hover.

title: tokens got their names, their art, and their whole history
body: covenant tokens carry no name and no art on chain, so the directory now shows Kron Token $KRON with its picture, without trusting anyone for it. names come from the launchpad's published list, and kascov checks that list against chain first: genesis transaction, the covenant holding the inventory, and the key that took the creator allocation, each already proven independently. the name itself is the one part nothing can verify, so it is the only part shown as a claim. art is witnessed rather than hotlinked: of 19 published logo urls, five were already dead and three were web pages, so kascov fetches each one once, keeps its own dated copy, serves that forever and re-checks the source daily. a changed logo is counted and dated, never silently swapped, and a witnessed picture wears a dashed ring so it is never mistaken for art proven against a hash. token history also reads newest first now, the whole life one page at a time.

title: the allocation a launch never spends is now proven too
body: a launch funds two cells: the curve's inventory, and an allocation the creator holds back. the curve trades, so a spend eventually reveals its program. the creator's cell just sits there, and a cell nobody spends reveals nothing, so 9 mainnet tokens sat unvalidated with one unresolved cell and their supply was withheld rather than guessed. they are proven now without asking any launchpad. the untouched cell's sibling from the same genesis runs the same program, so it stands in as the base: splice a candidate state into it and the chain's own commitment hash answers yes or no. every candidate stays hash-gated, so a wrong guess costs a hash and never a wrong verdict. all 9 resolved inside 120 hashes each, and every genesis pair sums to a round total. 26 testnet tokens came back the same way.

title: the builder guide moved inside the site
body: the 15-minute guide — compile a covenant, deploy it, spend it under its own rules, then replay that spend opcode by opcode — was the one page living outside the app, carrying its own copy of the palette and none of the site's navigation, search, or network switch. it is a page like every other one now, with a sticky rail on the left tracking which step you're reading. every link inside it goes straight to the thing it names: the playground that compiles the contract, the preflight that catches the compute-budget trap, the real coin on chain. old links keep working — /guide.html and its #trap anchor fold onto the new route — and the guide's text still ships inside the page instead of being drawn by scripts, so it stays readable to anything that crawls it.

title: a live page that stops moving under you
body: explore refreshes constantly because the chain moves ten blocks a second, and that used to fight whoever was reading. views faded out mid-read, the mempool strip changed height as it filled and shoved everything below it, a background refresh could wipe the deploy result you were about to copy, and each cycle fired the same requests two or three times over. now one gate shares an in-flight transfer and allows a single trailing refresh, views stay visible while new data lands, the strip holds one height whether empty or full, and the network you picked survives every navigation, reload and shared link. the pending feed states its own health too, so an empty strip no longer leaves you guessing whether the chain is quiet or the feed is broken. kascov also measures its own traffic from its own server logs: no analytics SDK, no cookie, no tracking pixel, no third-party collector.

title: the galaxy, readable at full density
body: the galaxy draws every smart coin and the moves between them, which on a network of tens of thousands of coins meant waiting a while for a picture too dense to read. it arrives in tiers now: the biggest clusters first for an immediate shape (?tier=core on /data/{network}/galaxy.json), then the outer geometry, then the identities that make each dot clickable. a dot never claims an identity it hasn't actually received — placeholder dots aren't clickable, and a tier whose layout no longer matches the identities it was handed drops them rather than mislabel a coin. focusing a small cluster at the edge keeps its surroundings in view instead of stranding you in empty space, the camera never zooms backwards, a click lands on the dot you can see rather than a generous invisible circle around it, and touch gets a target it can actually hit while still letting the page scroll.

title: watch covenants before they land: the pending lane
body: kascov followed only confirmed history. now it watches the mempool too. a per-network poller reads the node's pending transactions a few times a second, classifies the covenant ones with the exact rules the confirmed follower uses, and surfaces them in a live pending lane in explore. a genesis, transition, or burn shows up the instant the node sees it, then clears the moment a block confirms it, or fades if the mempool drops it. on a ten-block-per-second chain a covenant tx lingers only a heartbeat, so this is the closest kascov gets to real time. read from your own node's mempool, no third-party feed. GET /data/{network}/pending serves the current set, and the live stream carries pending and pending_resolved events.

title: kascov now runs on its own Kaspa node
body: the whole stack moved onto hardware I run and watch: a mainnet node, a testnet node, the indexer, and the site, all on one machine, off the cloud. it matters for what kascov is. every covenant you see is decoded from a node I run myself, not a public resolver that prunes deep history and abandons the cursor under load. it also unlocked the pending lane, because a live mempool feed needs a node you control. verify from chain, now from my own chain view.

title: trade buttons, from where a token launched
body: tokens launched on a supported launchpad now show a trade button on their kascov page. kascov works out where a token launched from an on-chain fact, the art host committed in the token's own genesis payload, not a handshake or a maintained list. KaspaRocket is the first supported launchpad, and adding the next one is a few lines. the verified art got tidier too: once proven against the sha256 committed at launch, the real image now fully replaces the generated icon instead of peeking out behind it.

title: a window that read 3 events, brought back to nearly 70,000
body: an outage weeks ago left a slice of testnet-10 history that every reachable node had pruned. a community node operator had been running an archival node through exactly that window and shared it. kascov walked their archive from inside the gap and merged what it found: close to 70,000 covenant events, back in the timeline, verified as canonical chain history rather than asserted. it is a big partial recovery, not a complete one, because even that archive had pruned some block bodies, and the recovery tool says so honestly. history you can check, not history you take on faith.

title: the art is real: hash-verified token images
body: a launchpad adopted the on-chain naming recipe within a day — real tokens now launch with their name, ticker, and image hash committed in the genesis payload. so kascov now renders the art itself: the worker fetches the deployer's image, proves the bytes against the sha256 committed on chain, and serves them from kascov's own origin at /img/{network}/{id}. match: the art appears over the coin's avatar. mismatch: it doesn't, and the page says why. nobody can swap a token's face after launch, and kascov never hotlinks a byte it hasn't proven. verified, not asserted — now in pictures.

title: real token names, read from the chain itself
body: a launchpad shipped with a verify-on-kascov button and asked the obvious question: why no real names? because kascov only shows what the chain proves — and until now, nobody's token name lived on chain. now there's a way: put {"name": …, "ticker": …} in the genesis transaction's payload at launch, and kascov reads it, shows it first, and badges it 'named on chain' — honestly labeled as a deployer claim, with the canonical name always alongside. the recipe is in the guide. names from private databases still don't appear here, and never will: verified, not asserted.

title: open doors: badges, a front door for the API, and honest timestamps
body: builders can now embed a live 'verified on kascov' badge in any README — /badge/{network}/{id}.svg re-renders from chain state on every fetch, so it stays honest by construction. the API grew a machine-readable front door at /data/{network}/index.json (production logs showed integrators guessing URLs on first contact — now a guess lands somewhere useful), every event now carries its accepting block's real header timestamp and blue score (stored since the capture migration, served never — until now), and share pages stopped shooing crawlers away, so the site can finally be indexed. under the hood: the shutdown backup now runs smallest-database-first so mainnet's snapshot always fits the grace window, and archives went hourly.

title: speaking the standard: KCC-1 template identities
body: covenant conventions are becoming a real standard — KCC-1, drafted by Romain Billot with Michael Sutton and Ori Newman — and kascov now speaks it. every conformance vector from the draft passes as a unit test in the new kcc1 module, KCC20 reveals carry their canonical template hash (3 identities across 2,889 verified reveals, each recomputed independently to check our own math), coin pages and the templates panel display them, /data/{network}/template/{hash} looks them up, and new spends record the draft's leader/delegator input ordering. tracking the draft honestly, not claiming compliance: it is a draft, and the vocabulary may still move.

title: the gap, healed — and an honest hole
body: testnet-10's frozen window is back: 60,789 events, 47,956 spends, and 48,469 state cells re-derived straight from the chain and promoted into the live index — 13,297 covenants got their history back. honesty where it's owed: the oldest slice of the gap had already been pruned from every reachable node before recovery could touch it, and that part is gone for good. the chart shows the hole rather than papering over it. this loss is exactly why the next entry exists.

title: kascov runs its own kaspa node now
body: production's testnet-10 follower now reads from kascov's own archival node over a private link instead of public resolver nodes — block fetches went from internet round-trips to sub-millisecond hops, catch-ups that took a day now take minutes, and archival mode means nothing the node has seen ever gets pruned again. mainnet joins it on dedicated hardware next.

title: the follower learned to fail loudly
body: testnet-10 froze for 49 hours and the dashboard said nothing — never again. the sync follower now probes whether its cursor is actually walkable (a block can exist and still be a dead end after a deep reorg), forces recovery when it's moving without progressing, and reports 'stalled' on /health instead of pretending. email alerts fire within minutes, backups stream every 5 minutes with verification (the old uploader silently choked on databases past 1GB), and a gap-recovery tool can rebuild lost windows from the chain itself while it's still within node retention.

title: will this transaction pass? find out before you broadcast
body: the playground grew a third mode: paste a transaction as JSON and preflight it — every input's compute budget checked against the classic 'script units exceeded' trap, masses measured against the block limit, an honest fee estimate, and a real script-engine run for inputs that carry their witness. every finding comes with its fix, plain as 'set computeBudget: 10'. your transaction goes into the call and nowhere else — nothing broadcast, nothing kept.

title: built with covenants — and a feed to follow it
body: the landing page now showcases what builders are shipping on Kaspa's smart coins, starting with the Kaspa Covenant Game Kit by @w00c00 — 1v1 games on player-funded covenant escrow, its contract verified byte-identical on kascov. and everything on this page is now an Atom feed at /feed.xml, so your reader hears the news before your timeline does.

title: every transaction gets a page
body: paste any txid — in search, or from any timeline — and land on its own page: which smart coins it touched, what was born, moved or retired, the cells it created and spent, the decoded token actions, and a one-click replay of the real spend through Kaspa's actual script engine. older workers still answer with the coin links; nothing breaks.

title: friends check each other's math
body: a new consistency endpoint cross-checks kascov's token accounting against other independent ecosystem indexers, automatically — token counts, supplies, the lot. differences usually mean one of us has a bug; we fix ours and share theirs kindly.

title: verified from the chain — not asserted
body: the accounting layer: every KCC20 token's history replayed, supply conservation checked, every live balance cryptographically proven against its commitment. 258 of 270 tokens verified, 0 invalid, the rest honestly marked with reasons. token pages show holders, classified mint/transfer/burn timelines, and the proof.

title: the galaxy glows and the front page breathes
body: coins are glowing orbs now, clusters are nebulae, the map sits on a parallax starfield — and the landing page's blockDAG is a living simulation: blocks born at kaspa's cadence, linking to parents, drifting like time. all of it pauses the instant you look away, so it costs nothing.

title: the mainnet galaxy tells the truth
body: small networks now show their actual coins — glowing dots with their shared-transaction links — instead of two giant summary bubbles hiding four covenants. click a dot, get the coin.

title: the chain has names now
body: the decoder learned genesis0, PURE and KCC20 from the chain's own revealed programs — thousands of covenant runs went from anonymous hex to real contract names, decoded and re-checkable by anyone.

title: the first open KCC20 token directory
body: every covenant token on the network in one table — owner and amount decoded straight from chain state, honestly badged "decoded, not validated" until the accounting layer proves them. plus USD context on mainnet and event filters everywhere.

title: an API worth building on
body: a cursorable event feed for the whole network, batch coin lookups, webhook secrets with signed deliveries, a live KAS price endpoint — and a builders guide at /guide: deploy, spend, replay in 15 minutes.

title: find, follow, replay
body: search all coins by name, id or contract from any page; coin pages update live as events land; and any real spend replays through Kaspa's actual script engine, opcode by opcode.

title: every coin link is a billboard
body: share a coin anywhere and it unfurls into a live picture card — name, avatar, holdings, story. plus a sitemap, so search engines can finally find the coins.

title: the big-network wave
body: the galaxy streams in tiers (big clusters first, the rest behind), the grid paginates instead of downloading everything, and quiet tabs stop refetching — kascov now scales past 168k coins without breaking a sweat.

title: analytics · the network at a glance
body: births against retirements over the whole history, coins by contract type, a survival curve, and the indexer's own reorg ledger — every chart drawn from the same feeds the page already serves.

title: make a smart coin without writing code
body: pick a covenant, fill in the parties and amounts in plain terms, and deploy it on testnet-10 in one click — byte-perfect script assembled in your browser, no toolchain.

title: a page for every coin
body: coin pages no longer depend on the loaded grid window — deep links, galaxy clicks and shared URLs resolve straight from the indexer, for all 168k+ coins.

title: the galaxy
body: the whole network on one zoomable map — every app at once, each dot a smart coin, each link a shared transaction. scroll to zoom, click a dot to open its life story.

title: kascov.io
body: the explorer gets its own front door — old links forward, share cards re-rendered, canonical everywhere.

title: first outside hands
body: community pull requests land — bug fixes from strangers and the covenant workbench unified into one playground. open source doing its thing.

title: the workbench wave
body: what-if spend simulation, cryptographically verified contract source, a visual script debugger, a ZK proof-verification panel, and payload lanes — the tools a covenant developer actually needs, in the browser.

title: contracts RUN now
body: deploy a real covenant, spend it, watch the program reveal itself on-chain permanently — plus escrow settlement, multi-contract app families, and a mission-control redesign with the BlockDAG as the hero.

title: stories get honest
body: multi-piece coins tell their true story, truncated histories get archival repair, "retired" is reserved for the story-ending burn — and a contract generator so you can make one yours.

title: the scale rework
body: the monolithic snapshot era ends: paginated grid, address pages, a live SSE event stream, template analytics and a daily digest. kascov stops being a demo.

title: coins learn to speak
body: friendly names, life stories, spend-time decoding that captures the program a covenant actually ran, and SilverScript recognition by skeleton — byte-identical, not guesswork.

title: day one
body: an acceptance-driven covenant indexer, a post-Toccata script disassembler, a lifecycle lab CLI, a live Cloud Run worker and a dashboard — kascov goes from empty repo to watching testnet-10 breathe, in one day.
